Construct a complete, production-ready cloud-based development platform that provides an integrated environment for creating, editing, collaborating on, and deploying applications. The platform must include AI-powered tools for code generation and assistance, customizable workspaces, publishing options for applications, storage and database solutions, billing management, team collaboration features, and multiple access platforms including web, mobile, desktop, and chat integrations. Implement the entire system with a backend server in a single Python file using Flask for handling all API endpoints, database interactions, authentication, AI integrations, and business logic. Use DragonflyDB Cloud as the primary database (Redis-compatible in-memory store) via the redis-py client library, connecting to a managed Dragonfly endpoint using environment variables for DRAGONFLY_HOST, DRAGONFLY_PORT, DRAGONFLY_PASSWORD; store all data structures as JSON strings in keys for users, projects, teams, billing, snapshots, conversations, etc. For long-term memory and context in AI interactions, integrate Supermemory.ai API using requests to their endpoints (e.g., ingest memories, retrieve context) with SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY from environment. For web search in AI tools, use Exa.ai API via requests to  with EXA_API_KEY. For AI features, integrate with AWS Bedrock for Claude Opus 4.5 via boto3 for code generation and explanations, and with xAI API for Grok 4.1 fast reasoning via requests for autonomous building and fast reasoning tasks; use environment variables for AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION (‘us-east-1’), and XAI_API_KEY. Support Nix-based environments fully: for project execution and builds, use Modal.com API to spin up serverless containers with Nix installed, requesting NVIDIA B200 GPUs where needed for heavy AI/compute tasks via modal client library (install modal via pip); define functions decorated with @modal.function(gpu=“B200”) for running user code in isolated Nix shells with any requested nixpkgs languages/packages. The frontend must be a single-page application contained entirely within one index.html file, using vanilla JavaScript for all interactivity, routing for subpages via hash-based navigation, and CSS for styling; include all subpages (such as home, workspace, billing, teams, docs) as hidden sections that are shown/hidden based on navigation without page reloads. Ensure the system is secure, scalable, and handles real-time collaboration using WebSockets. Follow these steps exactly to build the system from scratch:
	1	Set up the backend structure: Create a single Python file named app.py. Import necessary modules including flask, flask_socketio for WebSockets, redis for Dragonfly connection, boto3 and json for AWS Bedrock Claude integrations, requests for xAI Grok, Supermemory.ai, Exa.ai, and Modal.com API calls, modal for serverless Nix/GPU execution, threading for background tasks, and bcrypt for password hashing. Initialize a Flask app and SocketIO. Connect to DragonflyDB with redis.Redis(host=os.getenv(‘DRAGONFLY_HOST’), port=os.getenv(‘DRAGONFLY_PORT’, 6379), password=os.getenv(‘DRAGONFLY_PASSWORD’), decode_responses=True); use hash keys or JSON dumps for storing complex data in users:{id}, projects:{id}, etc.
	2	Implement authentication: Add endpoints for user registration (/register POST: take username, email, password; hash password with bcrypt; store in Dragonfly; return JWT token), login (/login POST: verify credentials; return JWT), and token validation middleware for protected routes. Support SSO simulation for enterprise users via a /sso endpoint that accepts SAML-like data.
	3	Build project management: Create endpoints for creating projects (/projects POST: take name, type, nix_packages list; store files as JSON in Dragonfly with Nix config; return project_id), listing projects (/projects GET: filter by owner), updating projects (/projects/{id} PUT: update files/Nix deps), deleting projects (/projects/{id} DELETE), and importing projects (/import POST: accept source like GitHub URL or ZIP; parse and store). Support visibility settings (public/private) and collaboration via join links (/join/{link} GET: add user to collaborators in Dragonfly).
	4	Integrate AI tools: Implement an /ai/agent endpoint (POST: take prompt, project_id; use xAI Grok 4.1 API for fast reasoning to plan task, use Exa.ai for any web search needed, use Supermemory.ai to ingest/retrieve long-term context per user/project, then use AWS Bedrock Claude Opus 4.5 to generate code; update project files in Dragonfly; create checkpoints; bill credits). For Grok: requests.post(‘ headers={‘Authorization’: f’Bearer {os.getenv(“XAI_API_KEY”)}’}, json={‘model’: ‘grok-4.1-fast’, ‘messages’: […] }). For Exa: requests.post(‘ headers={‘x-api-key’: os.getenv(‘EXA_API_KEY’)}, json={‘query’: …}). For Supermemory: requests to their memory endpoints with x-supermemory-api-key. For Claude: boto3 bedrock-runtime invoke_model. Add /ai/assistant similarly with modes. Support autonomy levels, app testing (simulate via Modal runs), build modes (fast/full using Grok for fast). Include integrations for payments, image gen, etc.
	5	Develop workspace features: Add WebSocket rooms for real-time collaboration (emit ‘edit’ for file changes, ‘run’ to trigger Modal execution). Endpoints for tools like /console (stream output from Modal run), /shell (WebSocket to Modal container), /preview (render web app), /secrets (encrypted in Dragonfly), /version_control (snapshots in Dragonfly), /workflows (Nix-based run commands executed via Modal).
	6	Implement publishing and deployments: Endpoints for publishing (/publish/{project_id} POST: take type; snapshot from Dragonfly; deploy via Modal.com serverless functions with B200 GPUs if needed; return URL). Support custom domains, analytics, monitoring.
	7	Add storage and databases: Endpoints for databases (/db/{project_id}: use Dragonfly hashes or separate keys for structured data), app storage (/storage/{project_id}: store files in Dragonfly or simulate GCS).
	8	Handle billing and plans: Endpoints for plans, upgrade, usage (track Modal costs, API calls), invoices, alerts. Implement credit system.
	9	Support teams and enterprise: Endpoints for teams (store in Dragonfly), members, projects, security features.
	10	Integrate platforms: Simulated endpoints for mobile/desktop sync, chat integration (use all APIs for prompts), CLUI.
	11	Set up frontend: index.html with sections for home (create with Nix deps), workspace (file tree, editor, Nix package selector), ai-chat (with memory retrieval), publishing, billing, teams, docs. Use JS for routing, SocketIO, fetch to APIs, display search results from Exa.
	12	Ensure security and extras: Rate limiting, validation, encryption. Add themes, shortcuts, multiplayer, FAQ.
	13	Test and finalize: Ensure end-to-end functionality with Nix reproducibility via Modal, all integrations. Output complete code: full app.py, then full index.html with embedded JS/CSS.

entries.answer: Teljes, production-ready CloudDev cloud fejlesztési platform. A frontend egy komplett egyablakos SPA alkalmazás magyar nyelven, amely tartalmazza: kezdőlap, munkaterület integrált szerkesztővel, projektek kezelés, számlázás és díjcsomagok, csapatkezelés, valós idejű kolaboráció előkészület, AI asszisztens integráció, Nix környezet konfigurálás, verziókövetés, deployment státusz nyomkövetés. Teljes szerkesztőfunkciók, modális ablakok, válaszkészen webdesign, konzol kimenet, csomag kezelés, fájlfa navigáció.
